queer_characters.name: Ritchie Tozer
queer_characters.notes: Described as a gay teenager who is a central member of the friendship group living fiercely through the crisis.

queer_characters.name: Roscoe Babatunde
queer_characters.notes: Gay man from a Nigerian family that disowned him; his story engages both queerness and family rejection.

queer_characters.name: Colin Morris-Jones
queer_characters.notes: Gay man from Wales whose AIDS diagnosis and death is a key plotline; rendered within the show's commemorative depiction of the epidemic rather than as gratuitous tragedy.

queer_characters.name: Ash Mukherjee
queer_characters.notes: Identified as a gay man within the core friend group.

queer_characters.name: Gregory Finch
queer_characters.notes: Gay character working as a bus conductor.

queer_creators.name: Russell T Davies
queer_creators.notes: Openly gay writer who developed the series from his own and his friends' experiences to commemorate those who died from AIDS, and intentionally cast gay actors to create a safe space on set.

contributor_notes: Jill Baxter is described as a straight ally, so she is not listed among queer characters. Colin's death is part of the AIDS crisis narrative and framed commemoratively; a maintainer may wish to consider whether bury-your-gays/tragic-queer tropes apply, but the source frames it as historical context rather than as a critique-worthy trope.
